transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I just can't seem to shut my brain off anymore. It's getting out of hand. It usually starts with just one small concern, like, say, a client not responding to an email. But then, within minutes, I'm completely convinced that I'm going to lose the contract. And then I start thinking about how I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and... and then I'm sure I'll just never get back to a real leadership role at work. It just spirals, and I can't stop it.
How long has this pattern of uncontrollable worry been happening?
It's been going on since I was fired... that was about thirteen months ago. I figured it would get better once I found some contract work, but it never really let up.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different areas of your life, including concerns unrelated to being fired or your divorce?

Yeah, it really is everything now. My mind just keeps jumping around. I'll be worrying about my current contract work, and then it shifts to how I'm going to make my mortgage payments. And then I start overthinking whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm damaged goods after losing my job. 

It gets to the point where... well, if I just get a delayed email from a recruiter, it can feel like actual proof that my whole career is just closing down for good. So, yes, it definitely bleeds into a lot of different areas.
Over the past thirteen months, has this level of worry occurred more days than not?

Yeah, definitely. Honestly, it feels like it's almost every single day. Um... there might be a rare day here or there where I'm just distracted enough that it doesn't get completely out of hand, but... yeah, it's definitely more days than not. It's pretty much a constant thing at this point.
Have you been having trouble sleeping because of your worries?

Yeah, it's definitely affecting my sleep. Most nights I just lie there, um, replaying interview answers in my head over and over. Or I'll find myself wide awake, checking the clock at 2 or 3 a.m. And honestly, even on the nights where I manage to get what should be a full night's sleep... I wake up feeling completely exhausted. It just feels like I spent the whole night on call for a major system outage.
Do you often feel keyed up, restless, or unable to relax because of your worries?

Yeah, I definitely do. I feel wound up pretty much all day long. My shoulders always feel locked up tight, like I'm just bracing myself for some kind of bad news. And I can't seem to just sit still. I'll catch myself pacing around the house, or if I'm on a call, I'm constantly bouncing my leg. Even when absolutely nothing is going on, I just can't seem to relax.
